findings.source: VaultHub.sol fund(): IStakingVault(_vault).fund{value: msg.value}(); LIDO.getPooledEthBySharesRoundUp(...); emit VaultInOutDeltaUpdated(_vault, inOutDelta)
findings.issue: The selector or the log word is stored through 'mem[mem[64]]' right after '_N = mem[64]', but read back as mem[_N]; the two are not identified, so 60 calls print a memory slice as their function name (some with their arguments decoded, so only the name is lost) and 19 events print their data as 'mem[_N]'. The same selector is named when written at a constant address ('call 0x0.unknown0103349c', 47 lines).
findings.rule: The address of 'mem[mem[64]] = X' is evaluated before the store, so after '_N = mem[64]' with no store to mem[64] between, the store is 'mem[_N] = X'; a later read of mem[_N len 4] or mem[_N] with no overlapping store between is the top bytes of X / X (no free-pointer range analysis needed).

findings.source: VaultHub._totalValue: inOutDelta (DoubleRefSlotCache.Int104WithCache[2]) copied from storage, then RefSlotCache.sol:162 _cache[0].refSlot >= _cache[1].refSlot ? 0 : 1 and :121 _cache[idx].value
findings.issue: The compiler's copy of a 2-element array of structs from storage to memory is printed as a while with a constant trip count (61 'while idx < 2', 9 'while idx < 64' zero-initialisations), so every later use goes through two memory indirections: totalValue's result is 'int104(mem[mem[32 * _8 + 224]]) - ...' instead of the storage fields of slots 2 and 3.
findings.rule: A loop whose counter runs from a constant to a constant bound (here 0..2) with a constant step is exactly its unrolled body; unroll small constant trip counts, then forward the stores: _8 = stor9EB7[v][3].field_208 > stor9EB7[v][2].field_208 and the value is int104(stor9EB7[v][2 + _8].field_0).

findings.source: VaultHub.sol:896 for (uint256 i = 0; i < _amountsInGwei.length; i++) { if (_amountsInGwei[i] > 0) { hasPartialWithdrawals = true; break; } }
findings.issue: The source loop is shown as a while, but as 'while True' with its own test as the first exit; _amountsInGwei[i] is raw calldata arithmetic.
findings.rule: 'while True: if c: (assignments); break; ...' is 'while not c: ...' followed by the assignments of that exit; cd[32 * s + p + 36] with p the offset of a uint64[] parameter is _amountsInGwei[s].

findings.source: keccak scratch of the namespaced mappings; PausableUntil.whenResumed; VaultHub._isPendingDisconnect: disconnectInitiatedTs != DISCONNECT_NOT_INITIATED (type(uint48).max)
findings.issue: Dead scratch writes are printed (the first two of each four-line group are overwritten before any read, P8), and the all-ones constant 2**48 - 1 is printed in decimal.
findings.rule: A memory store overwritten before any read is dead; print a constant 2**k - 1 as 0xff..ff (or 2**48 - 1).

notes: Small functions and the getters were compared line by line; the functions above 200 lines (setLiabilitySharesTarget, resumeBeaconChainDeposits, forceValidatorExit, burnShares, transferAndBurnShares, triggerValidatorWithdrawals, withdraw, connectVault, rebalance, voluntaryDisconnect, disconnect, settleLidoFees, socializeBadDebt, applyVaultReport (unknown146a9bec), forceRebalance) were reviewed by structure: modifiers and custom errors, the order of external calls (checked in detail for connectVault, burnShares, triggerValidatorWithdrawals, forceValidatorExit), events, loops; no semantic problem found. Source loops: only triggerValidatorWithdrawals' for. The pack lists ValidatorConsolidationRequests._consolidationCalldatas (two nested for loops) as reached by many functions, but no reviewed function calls it and the text has no such loop, so it is not counted. Implicit loops: 61 'while idx < 2' + 9 'while idx < 64' (copies of Int104WithCache[2] to memory and zero-initialisation of the pointer array), the address[] return encoding of getRoleMembers (448), the uint64[] calldata decode and re-encode of triggerValidatorWithdrawals / forceValidatorExit (3636, 3655, 2809): P7 74. Custom errors and events missing from the database print as selectors / topic hashes (normal). Calls to the namespaced-storage getters keep their raw slots; slices such as 'mem[mem[256] + 90 len 6]' (uint48 refSlot) and 'ext_call.return_data[12 len 20]' as a call target are P18-like. via-IR allocation checks (Panic(65), 293 lines) are real code.
summary: Complete and faithful, with the single source loop shown; the text is cluttered by constant-trip-count struct-copy loops whose results are then read through double memory indirections, and by selectors and event data stored via 'mem[mem[64]]' that are never re-identified, so 60 calls lose their function names.
